verdict.rationale: Glama documents a browser-based MCP Inspector that can test any MCP server, with no login required. It explicitly supports tools along with resources, prompts, sampling and OAuth 2.1, and can reach local servers through an mcp-proxy tunnel, so it covers exercising tools before integration. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the inspector works as claimed, and in-depth docs on the tool-invocation workflow beyond landing-page statements.

support.subject: As a developer, I can exercise an MCP server's tools from a browser-based inspector or playground before integrating it

citations.quote: Test any MCP server from your browser. Supports every Model Context Protocol feature, including tools, resources, prompts, tasks, elicitation, sampling, and OAuth 2.1.
Inspect any MCP server directly from your browser. No login required.
Test your local MCP servers with the inspector by exposing them via a public tunnel using mcp-proxy.
